bottom_line: In patients with chronic heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less, empagliflozin vs placebo reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.86).
implications: Based on the reported hazard ratio of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001), this trial supports that empagliflozin (10 mg daily) vs placebo lowers the risk of the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure over a median of 16 months in this population; it does not establish a definitive reduction in cardiovascular death alone (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.75 to 1.12) as reported here.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial in symptomatic chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, comparing empagliflozin 10 mg daily vs placebo on top of recommended therapy.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 3730 patients with class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to recommended therapy.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, analyzed as time to first event.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a compos- ite of adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospi- talization for heart failure, analyzed as the time to the first event.

major_points.text: Primary composite outcome occurred less often with empagliflozin than placebo with a hazard ratio of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.65 to 0.86).
major_points.quote: a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863 patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Total (first and recurrent) hospitalizations for heart failure were lower with empagliflozin (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85).
major_points.quote: The total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Rate of decline in estimated GFR during treatment was slower with empagliflozin than placebo (–0.55 vs. –2.28 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year).
major_points.quote: The annual rate of decline in the esti- mated glomerular filtration rate was slower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (–0.55 vs. –2.28 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year, P<0.001)

major_points.text: Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin.
major_points.quote: Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin.

absolute_effects.text: Number needed to treat to prevent one primary event during the trial period: 19 (95% CI, 13 to 37).
absolute_effects.quote: the number of          patients who would need to have been treated with        empagliflozin to prevent one primary event was        19 (95% CI, 13 to 37).

subgroups.text: Effect on the primary outcome was consistent across prespecified subgroups, including diabetes vs no diabetes.
subgroups.quote: The effect of empagliflozin on the primary           outcome was consistent in patients regardless of           the presence or absence of diabetes.

subgroups.text: Primary outcome subgroup results were presented by baseline diabetes status (HR 0.72 with diabetes; HR 0.78 without diabetes).
Primary outcome subgroup results were presented for baseline ARNi use (HR 0.77 no ARNi; HR 0.64 yes ARNi).

harms.text: Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin than with placebo.
harms.quote: Uncom- plicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin than with placebo.

harms.text: Study drug was stopped prematurely (other than death) in 16.3% vs 18.0%.
harms.quote: empagliflozin or pla- cebo was stopped prematurely for reasons other than death in 303 patients (16.3%) in the empa- gliflozin group and in 335 patients (18.0%) in the placebo group.

inclusion_criteria.text: Adults (≥18 years of age) with chronic heart failure (functional class II, III, or IV) and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less were eligible.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Adults (≥18 years of age) who had chronic heart failure (functional class II, III, or IV) with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% or less were eligible to participate in the trial.

analysis_methods.text: Primary analysis used intention-to-treat principle with data obtained up to end of planned treatment period.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary analysis was performed accord- ing to the intention-to-treat principle and includ- ed all the data that had been obtained up to the end of the planned treatment period

analysis_methods.text: Primary outcome compared using Cox proportional-hazards model with prespecified covariates.
analysis_methods.quote: Between-group differences in the primary outcome were assessed for statistical significance with the use of a Cox proportional-hazards model, with prespecified covariates of age, sex, geographical region, diabetes status at baseline, left ventricular ejection fraction, and estimated GFR at baseline.

analysis_methods.text: Target 841 adjudicated primary outcome events for 90% power to detect 20% lower relative risk at two-sided alpha 0.05.
analysis_methods.quote: a target number of 841 ad- judicated primary outcome events would provide a power of 90% to detect a 20% lower relative risk of the primary outcome in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group at a two-sided alpha level of 0.05.

analysis_methods.text: One prespecified interim efficacy analysis after approximately 500 primary outcome events.
analysis_methods.quote: This committee carried out one prespecified interim efficacy analysis after the occurrence of approximately 500 primary outcome events

analysis_methods.text: Hierarchical testing preserved overall type I error rate at 0.0496 (two-sided) after accounting for one interim analysis.
